english.title: Fail to remove hoarding, fence, platform or handrail when required
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), having erected a

(A)_[hoarding]_
(B)_[fence]_

at **(..SPECIFY LOCATION..) in compliance with section 172(1) of the Highways Act 1980, failed to remove

(C)_[that hoarding,]_
(D)_[that fence,]_
(E)_[a platform and handrail required under section172(3)(a) of the Act to serve as a footway for pedestrians outside that hoarding]_
(F)_[a platform and handrail required under section172(3)(a) of the Act to serve as a footway for pedestrians outside that fence]_
(G)_[**(..SPECIFY COMBINATION OF ABOVE..)]_

when required to do so by **(..SPECIFY AUTHORITY..), the appropriate authority
english.legislation: Contrary to section 172(3)(d) and (5) of the Highways Act 1980.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
fail to comply with requirement by appropriate authority
to remove hoarding, fence or platform

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Proceedings for this offence shall not without the written consent of the Attorney General, be taken by any person other than the person aggrieved, or a highway authority or council having an interest in the enforcement of the provision or byelaws in question - section 312 Highways Act 1980.
(ii) The meaning of "highway" is defined in section 328 Highways Act 1980

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level 3 on the standard scale and if the offence is continued after conviction, a fine not exceeding £2 for each day on which the offence is so continued.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
